curation.why: Identical to grammars/typescript's curation — the TSX grammar is tree-sitter-typescript's TypeScript grammar plus JSX, and every non-JSX decision there applies here unchanged: class_body is a wrapper; signatures and field definitions declare nothing nestable. export_statement is added as a landmark to match the built-in profile codemark shipped before 0.8.0: it wraps `export const handler = () => ...`, which is everywhere in TypeScript, and the generator can never propose it because the declaration it wraps is a child, not something it observes nesting. It carries no label, so it is never a container and does not add a breadcrumb level. lexical_declaration is proposed by the generator once the sample has an exported arrow function, but only as an unlabelled landmark; it and variable_declaration (`var`) are labelled `variable` so a query summary names them, as the built-in did. Neither is a container: the variable_declarator holds the name one level down and the arrow_function (labelled `function`) is the real body, so the trail shows the arrow function's line instead. internal_module (`namespace X {}`) is added rather than observed: a bookmark inside a namespace cannot be created at all (codemark#246), so the sample avoids them. It is labelled `namespace`, matching the built-in, and `namespace` is a container so it shows in the trail once that is fixed. `type` is a container, as in the built-in: a multi-line `type X = { ... }` has a body worth pinning while scrolling, and the sample bookmarks a line inside one. The generator does not propose it because an object type's members are signatures, not declarations. JSX additions: jsx_element and jsx_self_closing_element are labelled `call`, since `<LineRow line={line} />` is a component invocation (it compiles to a createElement call) and a use site rather than a declaration; jsx_expression (`{...}` inside markup) is labelled `expression`. None of them is a landmark or container. A JSX element has no name field — the tag name sits on jsx_opening_element one level down — so anchoring on it would produce a query that cannot be pinned to one element, and pinning markup in a trail would bury the component that owns it. The component itself (a function_declaration or an arrow_function labelled `function`) is what the trail shows.
